title: Naive search vs KMP
sub: Searching for aaab in aaaaaaaab: the worst case for the naive method.

frames.caption: Naive search: line the pattern up at each position and compare left to right.
Shift 0: compare text[0] = a with pattern[0] = a: match.
Shift 0: compare text[1] = a with pattern[1] = a: match.
Shift 0: compare text[2] = a with pattern[2] = a: match.
Shift 0: compare text[3] = a with pattern[3] = b: mismatch.
Shift 1: compare text[1] = a with pattern[0] = a: match.
Shift 1: compare text[2] = a with pattern[1] = a: match.
Shift 1: compare text[3] = a with pattern[2] = a: match.
Shift 1: compare text[4] = a with pattern[3] = b: mismatch.
Shift 2: compare text[2] = a with pattern[0] = a: match.
Shift 2: compare text[3] = a with pattern[1] = a: match.
Shift 2: compare text[4] = a with pattern[2] = a: match.
Shift 2: compare text[5] = a with pattern[3] = b: mismatch.
Shift 3: compare text[3] = a with pattern[0] = a: match.
Shift 3: compare text[4] = a with pattern[1] = a: match.
Shift 3: compare text[5] = a with pattern[2] = a: match.
Shift 3: compare text[6] = a with pattern[3] = b: mismatch.
Shift 4: compare text[4] = a with pattern[0] = a: match.
Shift 4: compare text[5] = a with pattern[1] = a: match.
Shift 4: compare text[6] = a with pattern[2] = a: match.
Shift 4: compare text[7] = a with pattern[3] = b: mismatch.
Shift 5: compare text[5] = a with pattern[0] = a: match.
Shift 5: compare text[6] = a with pattern[1] = a: match.
Shift 5: compare text[7] = a with pattern[2] = a: match.
Shift 5: compare text[8] = b with pattern[3] = b: match.
Found at position 5 after 24 comparisons. Most were re-checking a's the search had already seen.
KMP: never move backwards in the text. On a mismatch, the failure function says how much of the pattern still matches.
